slots.rule: The household whose electric car moved its use the most, with the supplier's inference set against it
slots.glossary: An EV home: an electric car arrives, and the supplier sees it only as more electricity on the meter.
slots.reason: No household in this run passes this example's checks yet. 6 households match the rule, and each fails at least one check an energy reader would apply: its electricity over the year after the car did not rise by the 1,750-3,300 kWh an EV adds (3 of 6); the car's effect its record states is not the 1,750-3,300 kWh a year an EV adds (3 of 6); it lacks a full year of electricity use either side of the car (2 of 6); it holds no electricity supply with us (1 of 6).

slots.rule: The two-rate (profile class 2) home whose actual reads put the most of its use on the night register, where storage heaters charge
slots.glossary: Storage heating: heaters that charge overnight on a two-rate meter (such as Economy 7), whose night units are billed cheaper.
slots.reason: No household in this run passes this example's checks yet. 162 households match the rule, and each fails at least one check an energy reader would apply: the record names no profile class 2 (Economy 7) meter for it (125 of 162); its actual reads do not cover both a winter and a summer bill, so its night share is not measured (81 of 162); it has no full calendar year of electricity on record (73 of 162); it has no winter bill on an actual read of its two registers to show (71 of 162).

slots.rule: The largest year-on-year rise in one month's bill through the 2022 crisis
slots.glossary: The 2022 shock: wholesale prices rose several times over, and the price cap and then the Energy Price Guarantee set what households paid.
slots.story: The 2022 crisis reaches one household's bill.
